articles.author: DG
articles.description:
During the Weedmaps IPO, my health burner was barely a pilot light. Friends burner was off entirely.
I told myself it was temporary. It wasn't. There was always another sprint.
The Four Burner Theory says you have four burners in life: family, friends, health, and work. To be successful, you cut one. To be really successful, you cut two.
Every technical leader I know has lived this tradeoff. We've just accepted it as the cost of ambition.
But here's what I'm starting to see with AI: it doesn't just help you allocate energy better across burners. It increases the total supply of gas.
Previous productivity tools compressed more work into the same hours. AI is eliminating entire categories of cognitive effort. And when that mental energy becomes available, you can point it at any burner, not just work.
I wrote about why this generation of AI might be the first technology that actually changes the four burner math.
The constraint was never time. It was always attention.
🔗 https://itsmeduncan.com/2026/02/18/can-ai-solve-the-four-burner-problem/
Which burner did you turn down? Is AI helping you turn it back up?
articles.title: Can AI Solve the Four Burner Problem?

articles.description:
The "Stopped Instance" Trap


Every AWS engineer has done it. You spin up an EC2 instance for a quick test, run your script, and then "Stop" the instance thinking you've stopped the bleeding.
You haven't.
While the Compute meter has stopped spinning, the Storage meter is still running at full speed. And if you're using high-performance storage or have elastic IPs attached, you might be bleeding cash without realizing it.
In this post, I'm going to break down exactly how an EC2 instance is billed, component by component, so you can stop leaking money on "zombie" resources.
This is the part everyone understands. When the instance is Running, you pay. When it's Stopped or Terminated, you don't.
  On-Demand: You pay by the second (minimum 60 seconds).
  Spot: You pay the market price, which fl…
